blocks.text: Light and other forms of electromagnetic radiation travel in the form of waves, which consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields. These waves are defined by their wavelength (λ) and frequency (ν), and they travel at the speed of light (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s). The relationship between these is given by:
where λ is the wavelength (in meters), ν is the frequency (in Hertz or s⁻¹), and c is the speed of light (in ms⁻¹).
The electromagnetic spectrum comprises of different radiations, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared radiation, visible light, ultraviolet radiation, X-rays, and gamma rays.

items: Only discrete amounts of energy may be emitted or absorbed by various atoms and molecules. Quantum energy is the smallest quantity of electromagnetic radiation that can be released or absorbed.
The frequency of a radiation and the energy it carries are directly proportional to each other.

blocks.text: The energy of radiation is expressed as,

blocks.text_alt: E = hc/λ (h in J.s, c in m/s, λ in m)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints E = hcν with ν, its symbol for frequency, and the unit cm⁻¹. With the frequency the energy is E = hν; the form with c uses the wavenumber ν̄ = 1/λ (in cm⁻¹): E = hcν̄.
